deals.evidence: En 2015, las deudas habían obligado al club a entregar el estadio y su ciudad deportiva al Gobierno de Navarra, que a cambio le cedió el uso de ambos espacios
deals.headline: Osasuna hands El Sadar and Tajonar to the Government of Navarra to settle its debts
deals.summary: Under its debt settlement, the club transferred the stadium and the Tajonar training ground to the Government of Navarra, which granted the club the use of both. The club has since been buying parts of Tajonar back.

deals.date_text: 2 March 2019 (members' approval); Navarra parliament guarantee 14 March 2019
deals.evidence: la junta directiva llevó la propuesta de endeudamiento de 16 millones a la Asamblea de socios compromisarios
deals.headline: Members approve EUR 16m borrowing for the El Sadar rebuild
deals.investor: Spanish banks, with a guarantee from the Government of Navarra
deals.summary: An extraordinary assembly authorised EUR 16m of bank borrowing for the El Sadar renovation, and the Navarra parliament approved a guarantee for the loan. The rebuild finally cost EUR 23,306,258, paid by the club; capacity rose to 23,500.

deals.date_text: During the COVID-19 pandemic; fully repaid July 2025
deals.evidence: se solicitó para hacer frente a las consecuencias de la pandemia por importe de 12 millones de euros
deals.headline: EUR 12m pandemic loan from Rights & Media, now repaid
deals.summary: Loan taken to cope with the pandemic; EUR 90,000 remained at 30 June 2025 and it was settled in July 2025.

deals.date_text: LaLiga assembly approval 10 December 2021; first funds July 2022
deals.evidence: Osasuna ha recibido ya 47.572.608 euros de LaLiga dentro de los 52.060.379
deals.headline: Osasuna's EUR 52.06m share of the LaLiga-CVC Impulso deal
deals.summary: CVC bought a share of LaLiga's media-rights business for 50 years; LaLiga passes the proceeds to participating clubs as participating loans repaid from TV income (Osasuna: over 47 years). Osasuna's allocation is EUR 52,060,379, of which EUR 47,572,608 had been received; EUR 44m was owed to LaLiga at 30 June 2025, repaid from TV income. Approved by LaLiga's assembly on 10 December 2021 with 37 of 42 clubs in favour (Heraldo).

deals.evidence: un incremento de deuda de 4 millones de euros derivado de la compra, al Gobierno de Navarra, de más patrimonio en las instalaciones de Tajonar
deals.headline: Osasuna buys back Tajonar land from the Government of Navarra for EUR 4m
deals.summary: The club bought 28,244 m2 at its Tajonar training ground back from the Government of Navarra for EUR 4m, paid in instalments, ahead of the EUR 18m 'Futuro Tajonar' expansion.

name: Club Atlético Osasuna
notes: Revenue is net turnover (cifra de negocios) for 2024-25 as the club's economic report gives it (EUR 68,190,047 in the control commission's report; total income including EUR 11.1m of player-sale gains was over EUR 82m). In April 2026 a new auditor (PKF Attest) found errors in the 2024-25 accounts; the club restated that year's net result from a EUR 2,058,747 profit to a EUR 1,605,097 loss (osasuna.es/noticia151). The original accounts showed a EUR 167,556 pre-tax profit (control commission report); no restated pre-tax figure has been published, so pretax_result is left blank. Wages are staff costs as originally reported, before a David Garcia salary item was added in the restatement. Net debt at 30 June 2025 was EUR 60,406,486 as originally reported. The 2025-26 annual accounts are due at the November 2026 assembly. Members: 20,100 for 2026-27 (osasuna.es). The audited accounts PDF is a scanned image without a text layer; figures are cited from the club's text documents instead. Not found: valuation (no published valuation of a members' club), attendance, social follower counts, operating result.

owners.evidence: El Club Atlético Osasuna es un club deportivo propiedad de todos sus socios.
owners.name: Club members (socios) of Club Atlético Osasuna

ownership_summary: Club Atlético Osasuna is a members' club (club deportivo), not a sociedad anónima deportiva: it avoided conversion in the 1990s and belongs to its socios, who elect the board and are represented by an assembly of delegates (compromisarios). It had 20,100 members for 2026-27. There is no private, institutional or fund shareholder; the LaLiga Impulso money from CVC is a participating loan from LaLiga, not equity in the club.
